findings.reason: adding a denominator plus a stated bound, or an explicit sample with its size, is a one-line change that turns the step into a measurement a reader can check instead of a count that may silently cover a fraction of the population.
findings.text: the closing step "runs the new reports.py reader over every `manifest.md` directly under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/*/` and records how many manifests change reading", with no bound, no total, and no completeness marker: a scan over that population took more than two minutes here and reported 19,387 `manifest.md` files, 541 of them carrying a commits line of two or more entry-shaped tokens, so a worker will either spend its budget there or report a partial count as the population, and neither the plan nor the gate log would show which

findings.reason: the scan found 541 manifests the split repairs, and every non-entry-shaped hit I sampled was a JSON-array fragment or a "none —" declaration rather than a sha followed by a subject, so the exception stays conservative; the population step is the place that would show such a shape, and the rule should not be widened before one is recorded.
findings.text: "a `commits` line of a sha followed by a subject keeps its present reading, because a subject word is not entry-shaped": the present reading is one entry, and an entry git cannot resolve is skipped without a word by `_require_commits_beyond_base` (promotion_evidence.py near line 276, `canonical is None: continue`), so that shape keeps exactly the silent drop the section exists to remove
